To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the germination process in pine seeds is associated with changes in mitochondrial enzyme activities.
the mitochondrial enzymes of germinating seedlings of sugar pine (Pinus lambertiana Dougl.) are activated by water absorption.
the mitochondrial enzyme system of sugar pine endosperm is activated as the seed absorbs water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the changes in the enzyme activities of mitochondrial particles during germination.
the changes in the activity of the Krebs citric acid cycle enzyme system during germination of sugar pine seeds.
the changes in enzyme activity which occur during the germination of seeds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enzyme activity of mitochondria from germinating seedlings of sugar pine (Pinus lambertiana Dougl.) is dependent upon the water content of the tissue and that the activity of the enzyme systems is correlated with the water content of endosperm tissue.
the enzyme systems of the mitochondria from germinating seedlings of P. lambertiana have been studied.
the mitochondria from the germinating seed of Pinus Lambertiana are capable of catalyzing the oxidation of a number of organic acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitochondria isolated from sugar pine embryos and seed coats were active in oxidative phosphorylation.
the Krebs cycle is operative in the endosperm of the germinating sugar pine seed, and that the oxidation of succinate by mitochondria is inhibited by water absorption.
we have demonstrated the presence of the enzymes of the Krebs tricarboxylic acid cycle in mitochondria from the endosperm of the sugar pine seed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enzyme activity of mitochondria from germinating seedlings of sugar pine (Pinus Lambertian Dougl.) is affected by the activation of Krebs cycle enzyme systems.
the mitochondria of germinating pine embryos have a high capacity for oxidative phosphorylation, but this capacity declines as germination progresses.
